summary: Aiko Okoshi was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University around 1970–1975. She was appointed as a full-time lecturer at Kindai University in 1990.

Aileen Dansken Ross worked in Indology and related fields. Educated at the London School of Economics (B.Sc.) and the University of Chicago (M.A., Ph.D.), she lectured at Toronto before holding assistant, associate, and full professor posts at McGill (1944–1970).

Ajahn Amaro works in Buddhist studies, having studied at Bedford College and under teachers Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho. He co-founded and served as co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (~1996–2010) and became abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery around 2010.

Ajahn Brahm works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Educated at Emmanuel College, Cambridge, and Latymer Upper School, he trained under Boonman Poonyathiro and Ajahn Chah. He became abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery around 1983.
Ajahn Khemadhammo is active in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the Drama Centre London and trained under the traditional teacher Ajahn Chah from around 1972 to 1977.

Ajahn Pasanno is a Buddhist studies scholar and monastic who studied under the traditional teacher Ajahn Chah around 1974–1982. He served as founding co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery from around 1996 to 2018.

Ajahn Sucitto is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who earned a literature degree at the University of Warwick and trained under Ajahn Sumedho from 1977. He served as abbot of Chithurst Buddhist Monastery from 1992 to 2014.

Ajahn Sumedho, a Buddhist and religious studies scholar, studied at the University of Washington and UC Berkeley, and trained under Ajahn Chah. He founded Wat Pa Nanachat, serving as abbot in 1975, and was abbot of Amaravati (1984–2010).

Ajay Verma specializes in philosophy and Indology. He completed an M.Phil. and Ph.D. at the University of Delhi between 1997 and 2004, and was appointed Associate Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2005.

Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied as a pupil under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya and held a post as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow at the University of Calcutta.
Akhil Rajeev P is a researcher in computational fields and Indology. He has held positions at the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing and the Indian Heritage Language Computing Group.

Akifumi Naito specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at Ryukoku University, Honganji Sōgakuin, and under Gadjin Nagao. He has held teaching posts at the Shinshu Institute of Doctrinal Studies, Ryukoku University, Kyoto Women's University, and Gyoshin Buddhist Academy.

Akihiko Akamatsu is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Paris/Sorbonne Nouvelle under Yuichi Kajiyama. He held faculty posts at Kyushu University and Kyoto University, serving as professor and vice president.

Akihiro Oda is a Buddhist studies scholar who was educated at Otani University. He later held academic appointments there as a lecturer (attested 1992) and as Professor of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013).
Akiko Kikuchi works in Buddhist studies and other fields. She studied as a research student at Minobusan University (attested 2026) and was appointed Professor at Musashino University in 2022.

Akiko Murakawa is an Indologist who completed studies under doctoral supervisor Harry Falk, as well as supervisors Gerhard Ehlers, Masato Fujii, and Muneo Tokunaga, and teachers Werner Knobl, Yasuke Ikari, and Kazuhiko Yoshida.

Akiko Walley is a scholar of Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1994–2001) and Harvard University (~2001–2009), and held a faculty post at the University of Oregon from 2009 to 2016.

Akimichi Eda specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. Eda earned a Dr. phil. at the University of Marburg (attested 2005) under doctoral supervisor Michael Hahn, and also studied under teachers Katsumi Mimaki and Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar.
Akio Donohashi is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo around 1967–1975 and served as a professor at Kobe University from 1990 to 1991.

Akio Minoura specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as an associate professor at Otani University (attested 2007–2013), completed research abroad at Stanford University (2012–2013), and is attested as faculty at the Otani Academic Society in 2026.
